final_message:
The `wolfi` and `chainguard` crash is fixed. For ids that aren't `CVE-` or `GHSA-` prefixed, such as `GO-2026-5932`, the parser now returns just the distro security page link. CVE and GHSA links are unchanged.

The cause was that `vulnerability.build_reference_links` returns `None` for those ids, and `SecDBParser.build_reference_links` in `src/vunnel/providers/wolfi/parser.py` passed that straight to `urls.extend`. I changed that line to `urls.extend(vulnerability.build_reference_links(vulnerability_id) or [])`. Chainguard uses the same `SecDBParser`, so the one edit covers both providers.

I ran the wolfi and chainguard unit tests and all 16 pass. I did not add a test for `GO-2026-5932`, and I did not run the full suite. The `.venv` doesn't have `vunnel` installed, so I ran those tests with `PYTHONPATH=src`. The command in `CLAUDE.md` fails at import without that.

I also wrote `answer.json` in the repo root with the one-sentence summary.

steps.command: sed -n 60,90p src/vunnel/providers/wolfi/parser.py; sed -n 70,85p src/vunnel/providers/secureos/parser.py; grep -n "def build_reference_links" -A25 src/vunnel/utils/vulnerability.py; grep -rn "build_reference_links" src/vunnel/providers/{chainguard,minimos}

sed -i '/^class SecDBParser/,$ s/        urls.extend(vulnerability.build_reference_links(vulnerability_id))/        urls.extend(vulnerability.build_reference_links(vulnerability_id) or [])/' src/vunnel/providers/wolfi/parser.py
echo '{"summary": "SecDBParser.build_reference_links now tolerates ids without CVE-/GHSA- prefix, returning just the distro security page link."}' > answer.json
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -3; git diff --stat
PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/unit/providers/wolfi tests/unit/providers/chainguard 2>&1 | tail -5; ls answer.json; cat answer.json
